findings.title: Any comment on the PR cancels the review run that is in flight
findings.why: The workflow triggers on `issue_comment: created` for every comment, and the single concurrency group `review-agents-<PR number>` with `cancel-in-progress: true` is taken by that run even when the `review` job's `if` later skips it. So a comment by anyone — including a non-collaborator's `/review`, which the action will refuse, or a plain comment — cancels the pull_request_target run that is polling the service, and its `post` job is cancelled too. The review result is never posted and the check never resolves, so anyone can keep a PR unreviewed/unmergeable just by commenting on it.

findings.title: A pull_request_target check run lands on the base commit, so `post` cannot be a required check for the PR
findings.why: Check runs are created for the workflow run's head SHA; for `pull_request_target` GITHUB_SHA is the last commit of the base (default) branch, so the `post` check is reported there and not on the PR's head commit. Required status checks are matched against the PR head, so following README step 3 / the template comment and making `post` required leaves PRs waiting forever on a check that never runs on their head, while the red/green result produced by the review is never evaluated for merging — the feature's central promise (D-037) does not hold.

findings.title: The https-only guard is bypassed by redirects
findings.why: Only the initial URL is checked with `startswith("https://")`; `urllib.request.urlopen` follows 3xx redirects by default and `HTTPRedirectHandler` copies the request headers (including `Authorization` / `X-Review-Agents-Signature`) onto the redirected request. A redirect to `http://` (or another host) re-sends the GitHub token or the signed body in clear, contradicting the documented invariant that no other scheme/host is ever opened.

findings.title: Rejected inline comments are silently dropped when the summary has no counts marker
findings.why: The rejected comments are inserted with `summary.rpartition("\n<!-- review-agents:counts")`; when that marker is absent `sep` is empty, `updated` becomes the unchanged `summary`, `_upsert` sees the body already posted and issues no request, and the comments GitHub refused are lost with no error. Nothing validates that the report's summary carries the marker (`gate` only looks at `report['counts']`), so D-033 ③ ("none is lost") is not guaranteed.

findings.title: GitHub API failures before the try block leave no result file for the post job
findings.why: Only the service calls are wrapped in `try/except Failure`; the PR fetches and the head check (`github.ok(...)`) are outside it, so a 5xx/rate-limited/403 GitHub response raises `Failure` uncaught, the step dies with a traceback, the artifact is never uploaded and the `post` job then fails on the download step. The reason never reaches the PR (no summary update, empty step summary), and the required check stays red until a re-run.
